avertissement: Traductions automatiques des textes français ; chaque nombre a été vérifié contre le français. Les documents de la Ville sont en français et font foi.

canopee.description: Tree planting, greening, fighting the emerald ash borer and heat islands.
canopee.enBref: The City buys trees and has them planted on public land, and pays an organization to green private and institutional sites. Boroughs add their own resources: money from the parks fund, rental of machinery, blue-collar worker teams. Exemptions also govern tree planting in two building projects.

etapes.texte: City council awards contracts to 7574479 Canada inc. and Terrassement Technique Sylvain Labrecque inc. to supply and plant 1,374 trees, then water, maintain and replace some of them. The maximum expense is $2,456,590.55, taxes included, for trees spread across seven boroughs.

Pierrefonds-Roxboro transfers up to $162,233.12 from its fund reserved for park purposes to the purchase of trees and plants. City council pays $3,071,550 to the Société de verdissement du Montréal métropolitain to plant and maintain trees on private and institutional sites from March 24 to December 31, 2026.

Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve authorizes an addition at 1620, rue Préfontaine with 25 trees and 5% greening instead of the required 40 trees and 25%. Montréal-Nord allows trees to be planted less than 1.5 metres from the street line at 5745, boulevard Léger, for a two-storey building.

Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve rents a mini-backhoe loader with operator for $152,916.75, taxes included, and sets aside $200,000 for additional blue-collar worker teams assigned to planting, from May to November 2026. Outremont entrusts URBEX Construction inc. with the renovation of the Parc Pratt chalet and the redevelopment of its surroundings, including plant planting, partly funded by the Programme de réfection et de verdissement des parcs locaux.

City council leases land in the Namur-Hippodrome neighbourhood, in Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce, to the Société de verdissement du Montréal métropolitain, for a total rent of $100 before taxes. The organization stores materials, equipment and trees intended for planting there.

aSurveiller.texte: The Société de verdissement du Montréal métropolitain must submit its accountability report by December 31, 2026 at the latest, then its report and financial statements by March 31, 2027.
The lease for the Namur-Hippodrome neighbourhood nursery runs until April 30, 2028.

deneigement.description: Snow removal and snow loading contracts, spreading of abrasives, parking by-laws.

etapes.texte: Boroughs are renting vacuum sweepers, tanker trucks, sidewalk washers and a mini sweeper to remove abrasives from streets, sidewalks and bike paths. Le Sud-Ouest accepts a bid of $272,352.78, taxes included, for six sidewalk washers with operators, from April 1, 2026 to May 15, 2028 [CA26 22 0006].

etapes.titre: Snow removal from downtown public squares
etapes.texte: Ville-Marie entrusts companies with the maintenance, cleanliness and snow removal of Square Viger, Place des Montréalaises and six other squares, including square Dorchester and square Victoria. The borough is also extending snow removal for the Quartier des Spectacles by one year, from April 2, 2026 to April 1, 2027 [CA26 24 0067].

Montréal-Nord pays for an additional grader rented during the season, and Saint-Léonard draws $200,000 from its surpluses to pay staff and buy salt and sand, after 39 spreading operations since November 15, 2025, while its budget had planned for 20 [CA26 13 0121]. Verdun offers to provide its own staff for the snow disposal site.

The City is extending by twelve months the turnkey snow removal contracts of Anjou, Montréal-Nord and Pierrefonds-Roxboro, towing contracts in four boroughs and equipment rental in Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie. Ville-Marie, Anjou and Ahuntsic-Cartierville are for their part extending rentals of loader-tractors and a grader.

aSurveiller.texte: Snow removal of roads and parking lots in the Grand parc de l'Ouest covers two seasons, from November 1, 2026 to April 30, 2028.
Turnkey snow removal contracts for Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce, Lachine, Outremont and Le Sud-Ouest end on April 15, 2030.
The turnkey snow removal contract for Le Plateau-Mont-Royal ends on April 15, 2031.

eau-egouts.description: Pipes, drinking water production plants, Jean-R.-Marcotte wastewater treatment plant, retention basins.
eau-egouts.enBref: This year, the City is funding and carrying out work on its water networks: water main and sewer pipes, replacement of lead service lines, drinking water production plants and the Jean-R.-Marcotte wastewater treatment plant. It is awarding contracts for the reconstruction and rehabilitation of pipes on streets in many boroughs. It is also moving forward the project to ozone-disinfect wastewater discharged into the Saint-Laurent river.

etapes.texte: The City is raising to $381,000,000 the loan that funds the disinfection unit at the Jean-R.-Marcotte wastewater treatment plant. The money is to be used to finish the ozonation unit, install liquid oxygen tanks and build the oxygen plant.

The City is awarding contracts to rehabilitate secondary water pipes without trenching, redo roadways and sidewalks, and replace lead water service connections. The streets targeted are located notably in Pierrefonds-Roxboro, Saint-Laurent, Ahuntsic-Cartierville, Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension, Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce, Le Plateau-Mont-Royal and Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve.

The City retains Pure Technologies ltd. to install fibre optics and continuously monitor 38 kilometres of prestressed concrete trunk mains for ten years. City council moves a step closer to a $951,000,000 loan by-law for the renewal of secondary waterworks and sewer networks from 2027 to 2031.

aSurveiller.texte: Announced adoption of the $951,000,000 loan by-law for secondary waterworks and sewer networks, on October 19, 2026.
Shutdown of sludge incinerator 4 at the Jean-R.-Marcotte plant in January 2027, for about six weeks of work.
Completion of the water main work on rue de la Cathédrale pushed back to March 2027.
Construction on rue Guy expected to continue until December 2027.
Commissioning of the ozone plant at the Jean-R.-Marcotte plant expected in 2029; contracts for lots 4, 5 and 6 are to end in the last quarter of 2028.

frederic-back.titre: Frédéric-Back Park and Saint-Michel Environmental Complex
frederic-back.description: The former quarry turned dump site, being transformed into a park in phases: urban greenhouses, biogas capture, electrical rationalization.

etapes.titre: Funding request for an east-west link
etapes.texte: The City is asking the Ministère des Transports et de la Mobilité durable du Québec for funding of up to $2,000,000 for a 900-metre multi-use trail crossing the park, with a footbridge of about 150 metres. The project also includes rainwater management structures and a 12.7-hectare meadow.

The urban agglomeration council approves construction of a greenhouse complex, valued at $2,185,000, then hands the project over to city council, which assigns it to the Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension borough. In July, the borough awards Les industries Harnois inc. a contract worth $499,865.92 to supply and install two greenhouses.

The City awards Systèmes Urbains inc. a contract worth $1,091,693.37 for the second phase of electrical work at the Saint-Michel Environmental Complex. The work includes a new 25 kV power supply, a transformer, a backup generator, and an automated system to manage biogas capture.

The borough awards Groupe MPotvin the redevelopment of rue De Louvain between the park and boulevard Saint-Michel, for a maximum of $8,199,514.82. The work covers sewers, water mains, lighting, sidewalks, cycling facilities, and plantings.

Two companies are awarded 30-month contracts for general maintenance and ecological and horticultural management of the park. The City also extends the rental of a compost screener and a loader tractor by five months, for $296,349.21 more; the compost is used, among other things, for park landscaping.

etapes.titre: Snow removal extended by six months
etapes.texte: The City extends by six months the snow removal contract for Frédéric-Back Park, the TAZ, and the soccer stadium, awarded to 178001 Canada inc. (Groupe Nicky), for $193,215.49 more.

aSurveiller.texte: The call for projects under the Ministère des Transports' funding program, for the footbridge and the east-west link, ends on November 26, 2026.
Installation work for the greenhouses is to be completed by December 2026; commissioning is announced for winter 2027.
The Boisé Ouest sector, 26 hectares, is to be added in 2027 to the 65 hectares already open to the public.
The snow removal extension covers the period from November 1, 2026, to April 30, 2027.
Work on rue De Louvain continues from May to October 2027 (sidewalks, curbs, bulb-outs), then from May to August 2028 (final roadway, bike path, plantings).

grand-parc-ouest.description: The largest municipal park in Canada, being assembled: land acquisitions, Anse-à-l'Orme, Cap-Saint-Jacques, Bois-de-la-Roche, parc-nature des Sources.

etapes.titre: More money for the heritage walls
etapes.texte: The City is adding $162,897.98, taxes included, to the contract for repairing the heritage walls on chemin de Senneville, bringing the contract to $1,174,331.77, taxes included. The file explains the costs through unforeseen site conditions: buried stones that must be cleaned by hand, additional mortar, sod, and a deteriorated culvert that must be replaced.

The City is submitting the application for the Cap-Saint-Jacques sector (330 hectares) for the international Urban Night Sky Place designation from DarkSky International. Submitting the application involves no expense; if the designation is granted, the City commits to producing a lighting plan, bringing its light fixtures up to standard, and keeping the site accessible at night.

etapes.titre: Two sectors listed as natural environments
etapes.texte: The parc-nature des Sources (38.32 ha) and the Anse-à-l'Orme sector of the Grand parc de l'Ouest (429 ha) are added to the Répertoire des milieux naturels protégés et contributifs à la biodiversité of the agglomeration, with conservation plans. The 2025 report submitted shows 4,051 ha listed or provisionally listed, representing 8.1% of the agglomeration's territory.

etapes.titre: Rebuilding of the chemin Senneville culvert
etapes.texte: A contract worth $366,117.31, taxes included, is awarded to Gendron Gestion Civil inc. to rebuild the culvert under chemin Senneville, as part of the modernization of the Bois-de-la-Roche agricultural hub; the total expenditure reaches $481,850.45, taxes included. The undersized culvert had been damaged by the heavy rains of August 2024.

etapes.titre: Snow removal, cleaning, and tree felling
etapes.texte: The City is awarding Paysagiste Solarco inc. the snow removal contract for service roads and parking lots in the Anse-à-l'Orme, Bois-de-la-Roche, and Cap-Saint-Jacques sectors ($178,330.82, taxes included), and awarding 9232-3914 Québec inc. the janitorial maintenance of nine buildings at Cap-Saint-Jacques ($704,619.24, taxes included). Entrepreneur Paysagiste Strathmore (1997) ltée will fell ash trees and other dying trees in the park, for a total expenditure of $1,713,041.27, taxes included.

aSurveiller.texte: Snow removal of service roads and parking lots from November 1, 2026 to April 30, 2028.
Janitorial maintenance of nine buildings at Cap-Saint-Jacques from November 1, 2026 to October 31, 2030, with a possible extension until October 31, 2031.
Felling of ash trees and dying trees from fall 2026 to early summer 2028.
Lighting management plan for Cap-Saint-Jacques submitted in February 2027, response from DarkSky International expected in April 2027, full site compliance by April 2032.

itinerance.description: Support for organizations, warming centres and shelters for people experiencing homelessness.
itinerance.enBref: The City lends municipal buildings to organizations so they can open warming centres, and it funds organizations that work with people experiencing homelessness. It also deploys a Ville-Marie public works team to other boroughs for cleanliness interventions related to homelessness. It is putting in place a framework to receive private donations and is appealing a ruling on encampments under the viaduc Van Horne.

etapes.texte: The City lends three buildings free of charge to organizations for the winter: the church at 5600, 12e Avenue to the Centre des Femmes de convictions de Montréal, the former monastery of the Recluses Missionnaires at 12050, boulevard Gouin Est to Projets Autochtones du Québec, and the Bain St-Denis at 7075, rue Saint-Hubert to L'Amour en Action SYL DAN. The loans end on April 30, 2026, and the value of the unbilled rent is estimated at $57,076 for the church.

Verdun pays $12,950 to the Société de développement social to keep outreach workers in its municipal facilities from January 5 to February 6, 2026. Ahuntsic-Cartierville ratifies the continuation of the contract with Les services de cohabitation sociale COHAB inc. for a warming centre for winter 2025-2026.

The City grants financial support to community organizations under the Programme itinérance et milieux inclusifs 2026-2028, for inclusion, public space cohabitation and awareness projects. The amounts cover a three-year period ending December 31, 2028.

etapes.titre: Private donations and fitting out of the Bain St-Denis
etapes.texte: Council adopts a framework to receive private donations intended for housing, shelter and social cohabitation projects; donors do not choose which project is funded. Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie transfers $250,000 for the activities and fit-out work of the temporary warming centre at the Bain Saint-Denis. City council also adopts a declaration of support for people experiencing homelessness and a motion on a rent support fund.

etapes.titre: Encampments on rue Notre-Dame and appeal proceedings
etapes.texte: The City awards a contract worth $149,520, taxes included, to Mission Old Brewery to support people from the rue Notre-Dame encampment area toward shelter and housing, and pays $90,000 to the Réseau d'aide aux personnes seules et itinérantes de Montréal for the 2026, 2027 and 2028 editions of the Nuit des sans-abri. The executive committee takes over the litigation on the encampments under the viaduc Van Horne and authorizes an appeal of the June 8, 2026, ruling.

aSurveiller.texte: Mission Old Brewery's mandate in the rue Notre-Dame encampment area ends on October 18, 2026.
The agreement between Ville-Marie and Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles for the public works team runs until May 15, 2027.
Support under the Programme itinérance et milieux inclusifs ends on December 31, 2028.

louvain-est.description: The neighbourhood being built on municipal land in Ahuntsic-Cartierville: acquisitions, soil decontamination, street names, temporary layouts.

etapes.texte: The City is extending the lease of a piece of land to the Société de transport de Montréal for parking its agents' vehicles, south of rue de Louvain and west of boulevard Saint-Laurent. It is also extending the lease of a neighbouring piece of land to a company for paid parking reserved for members of an app.

The Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension borough is awarding a company the redevelopment of rue de Louvain, between parc Frédéric-Back and boulevard Saint-Michel. The work involves sewers, water supply, lighting, traffic lights, sidewalks, the bike path and plantings.

etapes.titre: Main street becomes avenue des Solidarités
etapes.texte: City council is naming the new street at the heart of the eco-district "avenue des Solidarités." The name comes from a public call for proposals held in fall 2024.

The City is awarding a contract to build a road with sewer, water supply, roadway, electrical network and lighting in the eco-district, as well as for environmental soil management. It is adding $2,007,312.15 net, from the environmental liability reserve, to remediate the soil of the former gas station area on the Louvain Est site.

The borough is adopting a draft resolution authorizing the demolition of a building on avenue de l'Esplanade and rue de Louvain Ouest, then the construction of a group of buildings with a minimum density of 200 dwellings per hectare. It is also launching a draft by-law to increase the height and density allowed on part of the municipal land at 50 and 150, rue de Louvain Ouest.

aSurveiller.texte: The lease of the land rented to the Société de transport de Montréal for parking starts on October 1, 2026, for three years, at a rate of 92 days per year.
The free loan of the land for sunflower planting and the greenhouse runs from November 1, 2026 to October 31, 2027.
The free loan of the community garden land continues until December 31, 2027.
The land at the corner of rue de Louvain Ouest and avenue de l'Esplanade would be loaned for programming activities from April 1 to October 31, 2027.

The rue de Louvain worksite between parc Frédéric-Back and boulevard Saint-Michel continues from May to October 2027 (sidewalks, curbs, curb extensions), then from May to August 2028 (final roadway, bike path, plantings).
The street naming file indicates that site layouts are planned for around 2032 and that four other public places remain to be named.

matieres-residuelles.description: Collections, sorting centres, biomethanation and ecocentres.
matieres-residuelles.enBref: This year, the City is changing the days, sectors and frequency of collections in several boroughs, and buying bins for residents. It is extending its contracts for treating food waste and its ecocentre-related contracts, and awarding a contract to recover mattresses. It is also tabling the 2025 report on the agglomeration's residual materials management.

etapes.texte: The City is extending twice, by six months each time, its contracts with Recyclage Notre-Dame inc. to compost or biomethanate food waste from the eastern part of the agglomeration. The materials are transferred in Montréal-Est and then treated in Saint-Thomas-de-Joliette and in Moose Creek, Ontario, while waiting for the Montréal-Est organic materials treatment centre to come into service.

etapes.titre: Bin purchases and sorting equipment loans
etapes.texte: City council enters into agreements with Orbis Canada and USD Global to supply collection bins to residents of the boroughs, then with Plasti-Bac inc. for garbage bins for Ahuntsic-Cartierville and Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension. The executive committee approves an agreement with Tricentris, which is paying $43,773.61, taxes included, for a program to lend reusable dishware, water fountains and sorting stations at neighbourhood events.

The agglomeration is extending the contracts for garbage collection from front-loading and semi-underground containers, as well as the container contract for the Saint-Laurent ecocentre. It is awarding Recyc-Matelas inc. a contract worth $734,690.25, taxes included, to collect and recover mattresses and box springs from ecocentres, assigning two firms studies on buildings located on former waste disposal sites, and extending the contract for the software that manages dumping authorizations.

aSurveiller.texte: The program to lend dishware, water fountains and sorting stations is offered until no later than December 31, 2026.
The extension of the food waste treatment contracts runs until February 28, 2027.
The Saint-Laurent ecocentre container contract and the container collection contracts are extended until October 31, 2027.
The dumping authorization management software contract covers the period from October 12, 2026, to October 11, 2029.

namur-hippodrome.description: The new neighbourhood on the site of the former Blue Bonnets racetrack: sale of land, loan by-laws, waterworks for the Namur–De la Savane sector.
namur-hippodrome.enBref: The City is preparing the future neighbourhood on the site of the former Blue Bonnets racetrack, in Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce. It obtained an additional deadline from Québec to sell a first piece of land, adopted two loan by-laws for waterworks and public domain works, and transferred a piece of land to an organization for non-market housing. At the same time, it is leasing parcels of the site to organizations for temporary uses.

etapes.titre: Deadline extended to sell a first piece of land
etapes.texte: The Québec government grants the City a deadline until October 31, 2027 to sell a first piece of land on the site of the former racetrack, west of boulevard Décarie and south of rue Paré. The extension involves no financial compensation, and the other conditions of the 2017 transfer deed remain the same.

City council approves a City guarantee of $2,000,000 in favour of the Canada Infrastructure Bank, for a loan to Société GALOPH used to pay for feasibility studies of the residential project. The same day, council rejects a motion from the Official Opposition on governance and the management of assets and public funds in the development of the neighbourhood.

The City borrows $29,000,000 to develop the neighbourhood's public domain: soil remediation, sewers and waterworks, street redevelopment, fees and land purchases. It also borrows $12,000,000 to build main water lines between boulevard Cavendish, in Saint-Laurent, and rue Isabella, in Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce.

etapes.titre: Four buildings authorized on rue Namur
etapes.texte: The borough of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce adopts a draft resolution authorizing the construction of four residential buildings in four phases, at 7301 boulevard Décarie and 5150-5160 rue Namur. One of the buildings must house a municipal sports and leisure centre, and the developer must pay $3,200,000 for public amenities and equipment in the sector.

The City leases parcels of the site to the community cafeteria MultiCaf and to the Coopérative de solidarité Polliflora for temporary urban agriculture, as well as to the Société de verdissement du Montréal métropolitain for a transitional nursery. Each lease provides for a symbolic rent, and the organizations pay for development, maintenance and property taxes.

aSurveiller.texte: Deadline granted by the Québec government to sell a first piece of land on the site: October 31, 2027.
The federal grant of $128.3M is conditional on the infrastructure being completed by 2031; the funds from the $29,000,000 loan cover work from 2026 to 2028.
Communia has five years after the signing of the transfer deed to complete at least one building, and housing affordability must last at least 25 years.
End of temporary leases: April 30, 2027 for MultiCaf, March 31, 2028 for Polliflora, and April 30, 2028 for the transitional nursery.

parcs.description: Development and renovation of parks, including the Grand parc de l'Ouest.
parcs.enBref: The City is designing and redoing parks in several boroughs: soil studies, work contracts, public art and adjustments to projects already underway. In the Grand parc de l'Ouest, it is having walls and a culvert repaired, submitting an application for a designation related to the night sky, and hiring companies for snow removal, cleaning and tree felling. Several projects are funded through the participatory budget, the environmental liability reserve or park funds.

etapes.titre: Design, soil studies and funding agreement
etapes.texte: The City awards the winning team of a competition the design of the bibliothèque Caroline-Dawson and the redevelopment of parc Le Prévost, for a total expense of $10,559,257.81 including taxes. It also pays $174,471.56 to Verdun for studies before redoing the parc Monseigneur-J.-A.-Richard, and the Sud-Ouest signs an agreement with Hydro-Québec to obtain $154,000 for the parc d'Argenson.

etapes.titre: Grand parc de l'Ouest: work and protection
etapes.texte: The City adds $162,897.98 to the contract to repair the heritage walls along the chemin de Senneville and awards a contract to rebuild the culvert under that same road, in the pôle agricole du Bois-de-la-Roche. It submits the application for the Cap-Saint-Jacques sector for the Urban Night Sky Place designation and adds the Anse-à-l'Orme sector, along with the parc-nature des Sources, to the registry of protected natural environments.

The City adds $153,434.14 for work supervision at the parc du Bassin-à-Bois and $168,472.14 to decontaminate the parc George-Vernot. Boroughs shift or increase budgets for the parcs des Hirondelles, du Sault-au-Récollet, Villeray and Percy-Walters.

etapes.titre: Maintenance of the Grand parc de l'Ouest
etapes.texte: The agglomeration awards contracts for snow removal on service roads and parking lots in the Anse-à-l'Orme, Bois-de-la-Roche and Cap-Saint-Jacques sectors, cleaning of nine buildings at Cap-Saint-Jacques, and the felling of ash trees and declining trees.

aSurveiller.texte: Selection of the winning public art project for the parc des Eaux-Cachées in October 2026, contract with the artist in December 2026 and installation of the work in 2028.
Adoption expected at city council on October 19, 2026 to transfer a 75.2 m² laneway strip to the parc Le Prévost.
Start of the snow removal and cleaning contracts for the Grand parc de l'Ouest on November 1, 2026.
Response from DarkSky International expected in April 2027 for Cap-Saint-Jacques, with the lighting plan to be submitted in February 2027.
Final acceptance of the work at the parc du Bassin-à-Bois expected in June 2027.
End of work at the parc J.O.R.-Leduc expected in June 2028.

pietonnisation.description: Pedestrian streets, public squares and business animation ordinances.
pietonnisation.enBref: This year, the City is funding and overseeing temporary pedestrian streets on commercial arteries, mainly for the 2026 summer season. The executive committee paid $2,694,500 to the boroughs under the call for projects for pedestrianization on commercial arteries [CE26 0465], and the boroughs adopted the ordinances that close the streets, authorize terraces, sales, and music. Other decisions concern public squares: development, change of status of a lot, and official name.

etapes.titre: Grant rules and settlement of a dispute
etapes.texte: Ville-Marie adopts a by-law that allows it to subsidize its business development corporations to pedestrianize streets, up to $425 per linear metre, provided council closes the street by ordinance [CA26 240037]. Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie settles out of court for $41,686.46 a lawsuit related to work on the public square at the corner of rue Beaubien Est and rue Boyer [CA26 26 0010].

The executive committee distributes $2,694,500 among boroughs for pedestrian streets closed for at least eight consecutive weeks, including rue Villeray as a new project [CE26 0465]. Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce creates the Placette CDN from April 1 to October 31, 2026 [CA26 170058] and Ville-Marie bans traffic on the sections of its summer pedestrianizations [CA26 240090].

The boroughs pay contributions to the business development corporations organizing the pedestrian streets: $102,045 for rue Villeray [CA26 14 0078], $375,500 for rue Sainte-Catherine Est [CA26 240134] and $67,500 for avenue Lacombe until 2028 [CA26 170108]. Outremont allocates $105,000 to the pedestrianization of avenue Bernard, in addition to a $106,000 grant from the Service du développement économique [CA26 16 0061].

Borough councils close their arteries to cars and regulate terraces, sales and noise: avenue Bernard from May 19 to September 24 [CA26 16 0082], avenues Royal and Madison from June 1 to October 31 [CA26 170088], rue Ontario Est from June 15 to September 18 [CA26 27 0115], avenues du Mont-Royal and Duluth [CA26 25 0134]. Ville-Marie adjusts the dates of three pedestrianizations [CA26 240155] and Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve removes 113 paid parking spaces [CA26 27 0119].

etapes.titre: Public squares and end of season
etapes.texte: City council changes the status of a 899-square-metre lot at the corner of rue Sherbrooke Est and boulevard Langelier from street (public square) to local park [CM26 0888] and names the public square at the corner of rue Charleroi and avenue L'Archevêque "place Chez-Marguerite" [CM26 0913]. Ville-Marie authorizes sound ambiance on the pedestrian streets of the Quartier des spectacles [CA26 240372] and Le Plateau-Mont-Royal revises the reopening schedule for avenue du Mont-Royal [CA26 25 227].

aSurveiller.texte: Avenue du Mont-Royal reopens to traffic between Saint-Denis and Resther on September 30, 2026, and between Saint-Laurent and Saint-Denis on October 15, 2026.
The boroughs must report on the amounts received for pedestrianizations in November 2026 and return unspent money in December 2026.
The ordinance on sound ambiance for the pedestrian streets of the Quartier des spectacles runs until September 2, 2027.
The on-demand transit contract for avenue du Mont-Royal covers up to December 31, 2027, and support for the pedestrianization of avenue Lacombe up to December 31, 2028.

plan-urbanisme.description: The PUM and the concordance by-laws that each borough adopts to comply with it.

etapes.texte: Ahuntsic-Cartierville amends its urban planning by-law for the planting, maintenance, protection and felling of trees. Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie reviews its urban planning, special project and demolition by-laws, and Saint-Léonard does the same for its special projects and demolitions, after public consultations held on February 26 and February 11, 2026.

The borough extends its list of buildings of heritage interest, regulates housing and service establishments for people experiencing residential instability, and amends its by-laws on demolition, special projects and site planning and architectural integration programs. A public meeting was held on March 18, 2026 and a written consultation from March 11 to 18, 2026.

The borough changes the heights, uses and lot coverage ratio in the sector bounded by avenue Papineau, avenue Émile-Journault, avenue André-Grasset and rue Legendre Est. It also increases the permitted heights on sections of rue Lajeunesse, between boulevard Crémazie and boulevard Henri-Bourassa.

etapes.titre: Requests for extensions to the ministry
etapes.texte: Ahuntsic-Cartierville asks for twelve more months, until June 16, 2027, to adopt its concordance by-laws. L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève asks for six more months, citing staff shortages, the complexity of its territory and the fall 2025 election.

Ville-Marie amends its urban planning by-law and its by-laws on special projects, demolition, authorization certificates and cadastral operations. After the public consultation on March 25, 2026, the City reviewed the view corridor and height plans; the by-law allows a maximum height of 103 m on the block of the former terrasse Peel and requires approval for certain work in the declared heritage site of Mont-Royal.

Saint-Léonard takes note of two correction minutes signed on March 19, 2026, which correct the name of a school and the identification of a building on boulevard Provencher. Ahuntsic-Cartierville then adopts its by-law on building demolition, after a public consultation meeting held on June 23, 2026.

aSurveiller.texte: L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève says it wants to present its project to elected officials starting mid-June 2026 and hold a public consultation in September or October 2026.

The Minister of Municipal Affairs has set June 16, 2027 as the deadline for Saint-Léonard to adopt all its concordance by-laws; other blocks are announced, including the replacement of the zoning by-law.
Ahuntsic-Cartierville asks for an extension until June 16, 2027 to adopt its concordance by-laws.
Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension has until June 17, 2027 to update its by-laws; its zoning by-law must be replaced in 2027.

securite-publique.description: The Ville de Montréal's Service de police: contracts, neighbourhood stations, city council motions.

etapes.titre: Loan for equipment and loan of a police officer
etapes.texte: The urban agglomeration council adopts a by-law authorizing a loan of $10,880,000 to buy and replace specialized SPVM equipment between 2026 and 2030. It also authorizes the loan of a detective sergeant to the RCMP team that enforces the Firearms Act, for three years starting January 7, 2026.

The City buys 11 patrol motorcycles, extends the janitorial maintenance of the headquarters by one year, and awards work to replace the oil heating of the cavalry building, at 1515 chemin Remembrance. It also awards a contract for meals for detained persons and extends the maintenance of the call dispatch system software.

The City rents 50 parking spaces at 260 boulevard De Maisonneuve for headquarters vehicles. It renews the leases for the training centre in Anjou, neighbourhood station 15 in Verdun, and neighbourhood station 26 on avenue Mountain Sights.

The City enters into an agreement to supply 9 mm practice ammunition used for police firearms training, and extends the SPVM's mail pickup and distribution service by one year. It also retains suppliers for carpentry and painting services in the service's buildings.

aSurveiller.texte: "Fèves au lard" fundraising day at neighbourhood station 46, on October 23, 2026; the Anjou borough buys 62 tickets.
The port patrol boat and its trailer must be delivered by March 1, 2027 at the latest.
The lease for the metro unit premises of neighbourhood station 50, at 888 boulevard De Maisonneuve Est, begins on February 1, 2027.
The ACCES Tabac, Alcool, Cannabis and ACCEF committees are extended until March 31, 2027.
The work to replace the oil heating of the cavalry building must be completed by September 30, 2027.

transport-collectif.description: What the City decides around the network: land sold to the STM, areas around stations, agreements.

velo.titre: Cycling: REV, bike paths and BIXI
velo.description: The Réseau express vélo, bike paths and bike lanes, and the BIXI bike-share system.
velo.enBref: This year, the City mainly purchased equipment for the BIXI bike-share system, paid for work on existing bike lanes, and settled the occupation of Hydro-Québec land crossed by bike paths. Boroughs awarded maintenance and development contracts, and the City asked Québec for money for four new cycling projects.

etapes.texte: Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie issued an ordinance that formalizes the bike lanes on avenue Christophe-Colomb between rues des Carrières and de Bellechasse and imposes mandatory manoeuvres on motorists up to Jean-Talon Est. Outremont authorized $100,000 for de-icing salt and abrasives spread notably on its bike paths.

etapes.titre: Bike path repairs and sustainable mobility corridors
etapes.texte: City council added $3,400,000 to the contract with Bruneau Électrique inc. for sustainable mobility corridors in Ville-Marie and Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve, then approved Ville-Marie and Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension carrying out roadway and bike lane work, including repairs to the REV Lajeunesse between Jarry and Crémazie. Ahuntsic-Cartierville retained Déneigement et Excavation M. Gauthier inc. for spring cleaning of narrow bike paths.

City council awarded a sole-source contract of $4,815,802.61 to PBSC Solutions Urbaines inc. for bikes, stations and docking points compatible with the BIXI system. The executive committee then retained Laser AMP, a division of ISE Métal inc., for $394,851.17, to supply the steel pavers used as a base for the stations.

Outremont tabled a draft by-law to convert the shared lane on avenue Lajoie, between Stuart and Outremont, into a one-way bike path. Le Plateau-Mont-Royal awarded Cojalac inc. work on rue Parthenais including a BIXI station, and the Sud-Ouest awarded Groupe Damex inc. the development of three green alleys and the electrical installation of a BIXI station.

etapes.titre: Requests for financial assistance from Québec
etapes.texte: City council authorized the submission of four financial assistance requests to the ministère des Transports et de la Mobilité durable, for bike lanes and sidewalks on rues de Champlain, Saint-Jacques, Guy and Laurier. The City commits to paying at least half of the eligible expenses.

aSurveiller.texte: October 9, 2026: deadline to submit complete financial assistance applications to the ministère des Transports et de la Mobilité durable.
The repair of the bike path on rue De Louvain, between west of rue d'Iberville and boulevard Saint-Michel, is budgeted at $570,000 in 2027.
